name: Pak mod (asset replacement)
summary: Replace or add game assets with a _P pak in Content\Paks\~mods. Works without any mod loader.
description: A folder tree that mirrors the game's Content folder, and a script that packs it into a patch pak and drops it into the game. You supply the cooked .uasset files; the project gets the names and the folder depth right, which is where pak mods usually go wrong.

options.label: Mod name
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only
options.help: The pak is this name without spaces, plus _P.

options.label: Author
options.patternHelp: start with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, - and _ only

options.label: Game folder
options.help: The game's top folder (the one with the Engine folder in it). pack.bat installs the pak there. Leave empty to copy it by hand.

options.label: Game project folder
options.patternHelp: a folder name: letters, digits and _ only
options.help: The folder next to Engine in the game's install, the one with Content\Paks inside. Every path in the pak starts with it.

options.label: Pak format

choices.label: UE4, and UE5 games with only .pak files: one .pak
UE5 IoStore (the game has .utoc and .ucas files): .pak + .utoc + .ucas

options.help: Look in the game's Content\Paks folder. If it has .utoc files the game uses IoStore.

options.label: Engine version
options.help: The Unreal Engine version of the game. It decides the pak version and what the assets must be cooked with.

options.label: Folder inside Content\Paks
options.help: ~mods is the usual place. Some games only load mods from a folder of their own (see the game's modding guide).

next: Put the cooked files under the _P folder, at the same path they have in the game (see the text file inside it).
Put UnrealPak.exe or repak.exe into the tools folder (tools\README.txt says where to get them).
Run pack.bat: it builds the pak into dist and copies it to Content\Paks\~mods in the game.
Start the game and look at the thing you replaced.
